statement: Retention for the remaining unbounded tables, one table family per attempt: wasm_operations (the 24 h window becomes a delete, not only a read-side refusal), call_cell_reduce_results (published rows), control_plane_publications (one row per membership epoch and node boot; removePublication has no caller), the service install, revision, package, binding and module-manifest tables, artifact_payloads and artifact_payload_chunks (reclaim for UPLOADING rows), the debug session, breakpoint and snapshot tables, and schema_migrations with schema_migration_partitions. Each family gets a named owner, a horizon and a referenced-predicate, or an explicit owner ruling that its rows are kept as history with a stated bound. Size M.

constraints.statement: One retention owner per table and one deletion path (R01, R11). Retention rides an existing reconcile trigger; it adds no timer.
Each attempt changes one table family and its owner and lands on its own, so a regression is attributable to one owner.

A row is deleted only when it is terminal AND past its per-table horizon AND proven unreferenced by every dependency listed for its table (censused per family in this log before its attempt). Age and terminal status alone never authorize a delete.

Deletes are guarded and idempotent (R14) and run in bounded batches paced under the cache-tombstone bound (30 s TTL, 1024 tombstones per table), at background priority, so that load slows retention and never breaks correctness (R12).

A propagated table is never expired by time inside apply: that bypasses CDC and leaves every cache stale. Its rows are deleted through the owner gateway so each delete is a replicated mutation with its CDC obligation.
An existing remover with no caller (removePublication) is wired into the owner or deleted, not kept beside a new path (no-legacy rule).

Where rows are the installed-state or audit history a consumer relies on (revisions, migrations), keeping them is an owner ruling with a stated bound, recorded in this log; it is not a silent reclassification in the lifetime declaration.

control_plane_publications is propagated and written on every membership epoch: its deletion follows the epic deletion gate (three consecutive lab passes of the fresh-formation scenario and CDC delivery stages 1-3 landed).

A table moves out of class unbounded in solve/epics/system-table-retention/table-lifetimes.json only in the change that lands its retention owner, and the retained entry names that owner as file:symbol. The declaration is never edited to lower the epic metric ahead of the code.
Health and observability data is exposed through explicit collection functions, never a table (owner direction 2026-11-11); this quest adds no table.
The src/ changes land only behind an approving verification newer than the last attempt.
